html:
A Brazilian evangelical church founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1977 by Edir Macedo, a former lottery clerk who became its bishop. It grew into one of the largest churches in Brazil, with branches in many countries.

It belongs to the newer wave of Pentecostalism that spread fast in Brazil from the 1970s, drawing people from the Catholic Church. Its services stress healing, casting out demons and the "prosperity gospel", the promise that faith and giving will bring wealth and health. Critics have accused it of pressuring poor members for money, and it has faced lawsuits in several countries.

In 1989 Macedo bought the TV network Record, now one of Brazil's largest. The church also backs a political party and has elected many members of Congress, part of the rise of evangelicals as a force in Brazilian politics. In 2014 it opened its headquarters in São Paulo, the Temple of Solomon, a huge replica of the ancient Jewish temple.
